title: Spinal Ependymoma Investigation Network
summary:
Spinal ependymoma is a type of tumor that arises from the ependymal cells lining the central canal of the spinal cord. These tumors, while less common than other spinal cord tumors, present significant challenges in diagnosis, treatment, and prognosis. The genetic and molecular underpinnings of spinal ependymomas have been the subject of research in recent years, and one gene that has gained attention is MYCN, a member of the MYC family of transcription factors.
One of the challenges in targeting MYCN in spinal ependymomas is the heterogeneity of MYCN expression. Not all ependymomas exhibit MYCN overexpression, and within tumors that do, the levels of expression can vary. This variability complicates the development of targeted therapies. There is a need for large-scale, multi-center clinical trials to assess the clinical relevance of MYCN expression in spinal ependymomas and determine whether MYCN-targeted therapies can improve patient outcomes. Such studies will help validate MYCN as a biomarker for prognosis and guide the development of more effective treatment strategies.
criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Patients with histologically confirmed spinal ependymoma (WHO grades 2–3), Availability of complete clinical, neuropathological, surgical, and follow-up data.
Exclusion criteria:
Unavailability of complete clinical, neuropathological, surgical, and follow-up data.
